newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes slip on Iraq news, grades decline.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes slip on Iraq news, grades decline.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices declined Tuesday after Iraqi Oil Minister Amir Rasheed said Iraq exports would resume in a week to 10 days, puncturing holes in theories Bagdad would delay liftings into the summer,

Rasheed told a press conference in Madrid that he expected no problems in implementing the Iraqi aid distribution plan, a necessary component before oil sales can resume under the second round of the U.N. "oil-for-food" accord.

Cash traders said prospects for Iraqi crude exports worked against the outright price all afternoon, leaving July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing to talk late at $18.65-75 a barrel, 20 cents weaker than Monday.

August WTI/Cushing strayed little from the NYMEX screen, talking late at $19.00-19.10, a few pennies above the futures settlement. August held a 28-30 cents edge over the front cash July, with the roll trading at those levels, traders said.
Wednesday will mark the final day for July cash business ahead of pipeline scheduling. Traders said if Tuesday was any indication, the July domestic grades would slide out on a quiet note.
"As slow as it was today, I can't see anything much changing tomorrow, unless we get the outright numbers to move," said a cash dealer in Texas.
Sour crudes continued to defy some trader's perceptions of what a logical price should be, with West Texas Sour/Midland talked for July at 75-85 cents under WTI/Cushing benchmark.
Deals were scarce for WTS, but traders trying to peg an accurate price for August barrels were thwarted in trying to figure if the recent run-up in differentials would last.

"Look at all the foreign sours on offer in the Gulf. You have Oriente shopped around at $3.00-4.00 under WTI. Either Oriente screams into a $2.00 discount, or WTS backs out to $1.80-$2.00 under (benchmark)," said the trader.
For Tuesday, other domestic barrels were mostly quiet, with Midland talked late at a steady 20 cents discount to the benchmark, and Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James at 7-12 cents below the WTI mark.
Postings Plus hovered in the low $1.60's, and Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire at 45 cents under benchmark.
August Exchange for Physicals saw premiums slip further to only 2-4 cents over paper values. Absortion of much of the foreign crude overhang in the U.S. Gulf deflated EFPs.
NYMEX said on Monday that foreign crude deliveries against paper contracts tallied only 805,000 barrels, down from more that 2 million barrels against both the May and June contracts.
Weekly American Petroleum Institute (API) inventory data showed crude stocks off 765,000 barrels, distillates gained 905,000 barrels and gasoline levels gained 592,000 barrels.
